newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIAN OFFICIALS EXPECT TRADE WITH EFTA TO IMPROVE.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIAN OFFICIALS EXPECT TRADE WITH EFTA TO IMPROVE.

text.p: Lithuania's foreign ministry said on Thursday it hoped to expand the now low level of trade with EFTA countries, after a joint EFTA-Lithuania committee meeting.
"The turnover of trade between Lithuania and EFTA and Lithuania is not too big now," Algimantas Rimkunas, deputy foreign minister, told a news conference.
In 1996, Lithuania's foreign trade turnover with states of the European Free Trade Association (EFTA) amounted to just 625 million litas.
Lithuania's 1996 exports to EFTA states was 208 million litas and total imports were 417 million litas.
Lithuania's free trade agreement with EFTA was signed on December 7, 1995 and went into effect on January 1, 1997.

"We expect trade volume to increase because trade with EFTA is of key importance to Lithuania because it is an economic area with more or less the same trade regulations as European countries," Rimkunas said.
"Our trade with EFTA is an extension of our further relations with the European Union," Rimkunas added.
"We got a lot of interesting information on the position of Lithuania, namely being in the middle of western and eastern trading partners," said Rudolf Ramsauer, head of the EFTA delegation.
